item.title: New chief urges Vuda to prioritise education
item.description: NEWLY installed Tui Vuda Ratu Josaia Tuivou Tavaiqia has called on the people of Vuda to embrace change and prioritise education as the vanua looks towards the future. Speaking after his traditional installation at Viseisei Village yesterday, Ratu Josaia said education was key to progress and development.
item.content:encoded:
NEWLY installed Tui Vuda Ratu Josaia Tuivou Tavaiqia has called on the people of Vuda to embrace change and prioritise education as the vanua looks towards the future.

Speaking after his traditional installation at Viseisei Village yesterday, Ratu Josaia said education was key to progress and development.

He offered to provide land for a new school and urged other landowners to support the initiative, including improving teachers’ quarters and providing a new footpath for students.

He also urged the vanua to leave behind obstacles, embrace opportunities and put God first.

The vanua o Vuda transitioned from mourning to celebration after Ratu Josaia was appointed by the kingmakers or sauturaga, Yavusa Nakelo.

Traditional Warriors (bati) from the Tokatoka Werecakaca escorted the new paramount chief to his chiefly residence of Vunisei.

The transition followed the funeral and laying to rest of Ratu Josaia’s uncle, the late Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia on Wednesday.

Taukei Nakelo Ratu Josaia Natakele said the people of Vuda were happy to install their new chief, with many of the young participating in the installation event for the first time.

He said the newly installed Momo Na Tui Vuda, an American citizen, would stay at his chiefly residence of Vunisei for four nights as a traditional protocol.

item.title: Police boost security at Israeli Embassy
item.description: SECURITY measures at the Israeli Embassy in Suva have reportedly been raised in recent months, with the Fiji Police Force confirming the embassy requested additional police security. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe said the request was part of normal security arrangements provided by police following a security assessment.
item.content:encoded:
SECURITY measures at the Israeli Embassy in Suva have reportedly been raised in recent months, with the Fiji Police Force confirming the embassy requested additional police security.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe said the request was part of normal security arrangements provided by police following a security assessment.

“This is normal security arrangements provided by Fiji Police based on the embassy request and security assessment,” he said.

The Israeli Embassy did not deny that additional security measures were in place but said it would not comment on specific arrangements for security reasons.

“Israel and its mission worldwide operate in a complex and evolving security environment, facing a range of threats that require continuous vigilance and appropriate security preparedness,” the embassy said.

“For security reasons, the embassy does not comment on or provide details regarding the specific security measures and arrangements.”

This newspaper received reports that police presence at the embassy had increased in recent months and that Israeli Ambassador to Fiji, Maya Y. Yaron was residing at a prominent accommodation in Suva, where her room was reportedly being changed every night.

The embassy said Israel had reopened its regional embassy in Suva to strengthen ties between the two countries and their peoples. It said the mission aimed to share Israel’s experience and expertise in areas including agriculture, health, education, innovation and entrepreneurship.

Neither police nor the embassy disclosed the nature of the security assessment or whether the increased security was linked to any specific threat.

item.title: Hospital floor raises concerns
item.description: POTHOLE-SIZED opening in the floor tiles at Labasa Hospital have raised concerns about the condition of the health care facilities. The large gaps in the tiled flooring are located in what Assistant Minister for Health Penioni Ravunawa believes is the hospital’s laundry area.
item.content:encoded:
POTHOLE-SIZED opening in the floor tiles at Labasa Hospital have raised concerns about the condition of the health care facilities.

The large gaps in the tiled flooring are located in what Assistant Minister for Health Penioni Ravunawa believes is the hospital’s laundry area.

“That’s the laundry area, I believe,” he said.

The condition of the floor raises concerns for staff working in the area, particularly given the size of the holes and the movement of people and equipment through the facility. The damaged flooring could also create a risk of trips and falls if left unattended, particularly in a busy hospital environment.

Mr Ravunawa said the Ministry of Health was carrying out minor works according to priority.

“Minor works are in progress by priority.”

Labasa Hospital is the main referral hospital for Vanua Levu and provides medical services to people from across the Northern Division.

item.title: Decision upsets taxi drivers
item.description: THE Fiji Taxi Association has strongly condemned the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission’s (FCCC) decision to revert taxi distance rates to 2011 levels following recent drops in global fuel prices. This week the FCCC announced that interim fare adjustments introduced on July 1 to absorb surging global fuel prices, will expire on September 30.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Taxi Association has strongly condemned the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission’s (FCCC) decision to revert taxi distance rates to 2011 levels following recent drops in global fuel prices.

This week the FCCC announced that interim fare adjustments introduced on July 1 to absorb surging global fuel prices, will expire on September 30.

From October 1, fares will revert to previous rates, forcing every taxi meter nationwide to be reprogrammed.

Association president Mohammed Faiyaz questioned the economic logic of restoring a 15-year-old rate in 2026, adding that effective from October 1, the distance rate would revert to ten cents per 100 metres ($1 per km).

“How can a distance rate effectively set 15 years ago possibly reflect the cost of operating a taxi today?”

Mr Faiyaz said petrol prices remained roughly 31 per cent higher and diesel 45 per cent higher than in 2011.

“The $300 that a taxi earned from a given amount of work in 2011 is still the same $300 today because the distance fare has remained unchanged but the real value of that $300 has significantly diminished.”

The association also criticised the FCCC for forcing operators to undergo two costly meter recalibrations within three months, costing drivers around $50 each time alongside lost working hours.

“FCCC created this administrative and financial burden. It cannot simply send the bill to taxi owners who are already struggling to survive.”

The association called for an immediate suspension of the October 1 reduction, a retainment of the interim $1.40 per kilometre rate, and an urgent, comprehensive review of operating costs.

Mr Faiyaz said legal options and potential industrial action were being considered if the commission refused to reconsider its decision.

item.title: Father, son in custody
item.description: A CHURCH minister and his teenage son have been remanded in custody by the Sigatoka Magistrate’s Court over their alleged involvement in the death of a man along the Queens Highway on August 2. Fifty-one-year-old Ratu Vula Maimuri Ratuva and his 19-year-old son, Ratu Kinijoji Ranovo Ratuva, appeared before Magistrate Veniana Diroiroi yesterday jointly charged with one count of murder and one count
item.content:encoded:
A CHURCH minister and his teenage son have been remanded in custody by the Sigatoka Magistrate’s Court over their alleged involvement in the death of a man along the Queens Highway on August 2.

Fifty-one-year-old Ratu Vula Maimuri Ratuva and his 19-year-old son, Ratu Kinijoji Ranovo Ratuva, appeared before Magistrate Veniana Diroiroi yesterday jointly charged with one count of murder and one count of assault.

Ratu Kinijoji faces an additional charge of assault.

The charges stem from an alleged confrontation that took place between Kulukulu and Naqere in Nadroga on Sunday, August 2.

Police allege the accused pair, who were looking for three missing horses, confronted Vimal Nand, his son, and another student while they were riding horses.

Mr Nand was later found unconscious by his brother, suffering from severe head injuries.

He was rushed to the Sigatoka Hospital, transferred to Nadi, and subsequently moved to the Lautoka Aspen Hospital, where he died.

Police prosecutor Inspector Shamim Hassan strongly objected to bail, telling the court that Ratu Vula failed in his duty to keep the peace by accompanying his son to assault the victim instead of reporting the three missing horses to police.

Inspector Hassan submitted that the alleged incident occurred in front of the victim’s son and raised significant public interest concerns.

Defence lawyer Lauvula Korotamudu informed the court that full disclosures, including caution interviews and the post-mortem examination report, were yet to be served.

She told the court her clients run a horse-riding business and had approached Mr Nand near where their animals had disappeared.

Ms Korotamudu said the matter would not have escalated had the victim not fled, and also questioned claims that alcohol was involved.

Magistrate Diroiroi remanded both men in custody and transferred the case to the High Court in Lautoka.

item.title: Accessible tourism – Operator: Significant potential for this travel market in Fiji
item.description: THE Rosie Travel Group has signed an agreement with the Australian government-funded Market Development Facility (MDF) to expand Fiji’s accessible and inclusive tourism market, with a focus on travellers from Australia and New Zealand. Demand for accessible travel is growing across Australasia, driven by an ageing population, multi-generational travel and rising expectations for inclusive visitor
item.content:encoded:
THE Rosie Travel Group has signed an agreement with the Australian government-funded Market Development Facility (MDF) to expand Fiji’s accessible and inclusive tourism market, with a focus on travellers from Australia and New Zealand.

Demand for accessible travel is growing across Australasia, driven by an ageing population, multi-generational travel and rising expectations for inclusive visitor experiences.

Tourism Research Australia reported that accessible tourism generated a record $AU29.2 billion (approx $F49.6b) in expenditure across 70.5 million trips in 2024.

As part of the initiative, Rosie Travel Group has launched AccessibleFiji.com, a destination platform aimed at increasing awareness of accessible tourism options, supporting accessibility assessments and promoting inclusive travel experiences across Fiji.

Rosie Travel Group group general manager Eroni Puamau said Fiji had significant potential to grow its accessible and inclusive travel market.

“AccessibleFiji.com is a very deliberate strategy to tap the huge potential for Fiji and to do it properly,” Mr Puamau said.

“And so, it is very important that we build our awareness of what this traveller requires in terms of handling and service.”

The partnership will also support Fiji’s first Accessible Travel Awareness Workshop for the tourism industry, to be held from September 23-25 at the Tanoa International Hotel in Nadi.

The workshop will be delivered by the Global Sustainable Tourism Council (GSTC) and will focus on accessible travel standards, customer needs and service delivery.

Under the partnership, MDF will also support Rosie Travel Group to strengthen local training capacity through the Rosie Academy.

The program will help tourism businesses develop the skills and knowledge needed to better serve travellers with diverse access requirements.

Following the workshop, Rosie Travel Group staff are expected to become GSTC-certified trainers, enabling them to deliver accessible tourism training and accreditation.

MDF Fiji country director Kelera Cavuilati said accessible tourism could strengthen Fiji’s tourism sector while also making it possible for more people to experience the country.

“Making tourism more accessible and inclusive benefits everyone,” Ms Cavuilati said.

“It opens opportunities for more people to experience Fiji, while helping businesses better meet the needs of a changing visitor market.

“Rosie Travel Group is showing leadership in this space, and we’re pleased to support an initiative that can help build awareness and capability across the industry.”

The partnership reflects a growing commitment to ensuring Fiji’s tourism sector evolves to meet the needs of a changing visitor market.

By building local expertise, strengthening industry awareness and promoting accessible travel experiences, Rosie Travel Group and MDF are helping lay the foundations for a more inclusive and competitive tourism industry for Fiji.

item.title: Littering fine jumps from $40 to $200 from September
item.description: People caught littering in Fiji will face a significantly higher penalty from September 1, with the fixed fine increasing five-fold from $40 to $200. Cabinet has endorsed the Litter Offence (Fixed Penalty Notice) (Amendment) Regulations 2026, strengthening the country’s enforcement framework for litter offences.
item.content:encoded:
People caught littering in Fiji will face a significantly higher penalty from September 1, with the fixed fine increasing five-fold from $40 to $200.

Cabinet has endorsed the Litter Offence (Fixed Penalty Notice) (Amendment) Regulations 2026, strengthening the country’s enforcement framework for litter offences.

The new $200 penalty will take effect from September 1, 2026.

The amended regulations are intended to address enforcement gaps, outdated penalties and procedural weaknesses under the existing system.

Government says the changes will establish a more consistent nationwide approach for Litter Prevention Officers, municipal councils and other authorised enforcement officers dealing with litter offences.

The strengthened framework will also include training for enforcement officers and improved administrative arrangements aimed at making enforcement more effective.

Digital payment mechanisms will be introduced for Fixed Penalty Notices, while increased public awareness will form part of preparations for the new regime.

The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change and relevant enforcement agencies will undertake preparatory work ahead of the September implementation.

The increase means the fixed penalty for littering will rise by $160, from $40 to $200, as authorities move to strengthen deterrence and enforcement against littering across the country.

item.title: Adjust your LEDs – LTA warns of fines for dazzling lights
item.description: THE growing number of complaints about dazzling headlights has prompted the Land Transport Authority to remind motorists that LED headlights are permitted, provided they do not create undue glare for other road users. The clarification from the authority comes amid growing public concern over dazzling headlights, stressing that the issue is not the use of LED lights themselves, but whether they ar
item.content:encoded:
THE growing number of complaints about dazzling headlights has prompted the Land Transport Authority to remind motorists that LED headlights are permitted, provided they do not create undue glare for other road users.

The clarification from the authority comes amid growing public concern over dazzling headlights, stressing that the issue is not the use of LED lights themselves, but whether they are adjusted and used in accordance with the law.

Authority CEO Irimaia Rokosawa said the installation and use of vehicle headlights were governed by Regulation 57 of the Land Transport Act (Vehicle Registration and Construction) Regulations 2000.

“The regulation does not prohibit the use of LED headlights as many vehicles manufactured today are fitted with LED headlamps,” he said.

“However, under the relevant regulatory provisions, the low beam of the vehicle must be aimed so as not to produce undue glare forward of and to the right of the vehicle.”

Mr Rokosawa said there were currently no regulated limits on the brightness of headlights.

He said the authority recorded an increase in complaints relating to non-conforming LED lights, particularly those that produced excessive glare and compromised visibility for other road users.

“The enforcement team has strengthened monitoring efforts and is actively issuing Traffic Infringement Notices to motorists found operating vehicles fitted with non-compliant lighting systems.”

He said motorists with illegal LED lights or excessively dark window tint could also be issued call back slips requiring them to present their vehicles for inspection after defects had been rectified.

He said the authority would continue targeted enforcement operations to ensure vehicles complied with legal provisions, safety standards and vehicle compliance requirements.
